Hanoi, Vietnam14 contributions

a mixed bag
Sep 2020
There are pros and cons to Essie, I suppose what you want in a teahouse and bistro will influence how you feel about it. As far as the tea and coffee go, they are all very good, the service is excellent and always with a smile. The food is hit and miss, sometimes excellent, sometimes not. Usually not particularly fast, but whatever. I think that the management needs to take an objective, hard look at first impressions though. The table runners and little textiles that the silverware come in are absolutely filthy. The chair upholstery could do with a good scrub too. I'm ok with rustic, shabby chic, but eating establishments have to be clean, and this place is just dirty, from the fixtures to the decorations to the salt and pepper shakers, they all look like no one has been instructed to have a good go at them....ever. I shutter to think of what the kitchen looks like. As I implied, I blame this on management, employees will only behave as they are trained to.

Inspiring place, Unique designed tea house
Mar 2020 • Business
Unique designed tea house and restaurant in beautiful colonial house, with inviting patio shadowed by fruit and palm trees, in quiet street in Hanoi.

Relaxing and inspiring place thanks to the love to detail and good taste how it has been furnished.

My food, a sizable, high quality piece of beef was served exactly as ordered (medium), tender and delicious by very attentive and friendly staff. It came with tasty potato, vegetables and 2 selection of sauce.

The entree mushroom cream was also very tasty.

Prices are ok.

I recommend the place for romantic dinners, group events or just for an afternoon coffee or tea. They also serve breakfast and sell tea and tea accessories in their own little shop.

An unforgettable experience. Thanks to the staff and the manager.

I will be going again.

A bit pricey but a tasteful and relaxing spot
Apr 2019 • Friends
I'll be honest, I'd specifically not visited Essie because of the prices. However, when some friends suggested it, I went along. It's certainly a bit pricier than the average fare in Tay Ho, it's actually quite a good spot. The tea was served properly (loose leaf) which was nice. It annoys me to pay USD 2-3 for a single teabag and a cup of hot water. This was not that. This was a real tea experience and even miserly me enjoyed drinking tea out of a proper tea cup rather than a coffee mug. The feeling in my hand did make a difference. 

We were on their front patio but I'm told that the upstairs room also has a nice view!

Such a cute spot!
Nov 2018 • Couples
Came here for breakfast with my husband. He had a vietnamese coffee with milk and the huevos rancheros breakfast. The coffee was the best he has had so far i. Vietnam. The rancheros was good but we have had better in Mexico and California - no surprise there! I had a small pot of the coconut black tea with milk which came steamed. The tea set was adorable and delicious! I had the herb omelette which was served with 4 warm slices of a baguette - very good. We shared the mulberry crepe which was excellent. Overall a very cute location with good food and great service. Would definitely go back!
